key_insight: Across six LLMs, smoking-cessation advice varied by user persona; a factual-floor system prompt reduced these differences but did not consistently improve overall fact coverage.
engineering_relevance: Health-advice systems need model-specific validation of age-aware factual safeguards while allowing tone and vocabulary to adapt to users.
method: Asked six LLMs from four providers the same four cessation questions using 12 personas.
Audited factual coverage across personas differing in life stage, expertise, and smoking history.
Tested a short system prompt specifying core medical facts to include when relevant.
evidence_signal: Across 2,880 responses, every model mentioned FDA-approved prescription cessation medications less often for teen than adult personas, by 32–67 percentage points; five of six provided fewer facts to a healthcare-expert persona than to one presenting no expertise.
watch_item: Persona differences do not isolate individual attributes, and equal medication mention rates are not necessarily clinically appropriate because prescription cessation pharmacotherapy is not recommended for minors.
paper_title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
